summary: Iteration 28: Verified NEW-patient acceptance flow end-to-end (backend + frontend). Physician Accept button label is 'Accept' for new_patient and 'Accept back to practice' for former_return; WAITING_LIST filter (data-testid app-filter-WAITING_LIST) exists and filters correctly. Accepting a new_patient application via PATCH /api/internal/applications/{id} {action:'accept'} creates users(role=patient, pending_activation=true), patients(verification_status=verified, 4-digit visita_patient_id), patient_directory(patient_status=ACTIVE, linked_patient_id) and account_activations row. POST /api/auth/activate/validate returns {ok, email, name} for a valid token and 400 for bad/used/expired; POST /api/auth/activate rejects password<8 (400), succeeds with {token,user(role=patient)} and is single-use (2nd call 400). Login with new password works. GET /api/portal/overview after activation includes 'Welcome to VIen EMR' notification. UI /activate?uid&token=BAD shows data-testid activate-invalid with 'Go to Sign in'; with valid token shows activate-form and after submitting matching >=8 char password redirects to /portal (auto-login). Former-return acceptance flips matched directory to ACTIVE and does NOT create a new user (regression preserved). Backend pytest: 10/10 passed. Frontend UI test: all assertions passed. Note: physician password Newman2013_! works (must_change_password gate not blocking).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py ~2892 lines - continue trend toward router splits (auth, applications, portal, internal) for maintainability.

_accept_new_patient sends activation email inside the accept handler; if email delivery fails it only logs a warning. Acceptable given the token is still in DB, but consider surfacing a 'resend activation email' internal action if this becomes a support pattern.
account_activation link only sent when APP_BASE_URL starts with https:// — good gate. Also verify APP_BASE_URL is set in production .env before enabling for real patients.

_valid_activation compares expires_at using fromisoformat but stores ISO with tz — works because .isoformat() on aware datetime keeps tz; keep both writers tz-aware to avoid naive/aware comparison ValueError.
